stem: If \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\), \(m\angle B = 60^\circ\), then \(m\angle E =\) ________.
solution: **(B)** \(60^\circ\). Corresponding angles of similar triangles are congruent. In the correspondence \(ABC \leftrightarrow DEF\), vertex \(E\) corresponds to vertex \(B\). \(\therefore m\angle E = m\angle B = 60^\circ\).

stem: Two circles of radii 5.5 cm and 4.2 cm touch each other externally then distance between their centres is ________.
solution: **(A)** 9.7 cm. When two circles touch each other externally, the distance between their centres is the sum of their radii. \(\therefore\) distance \(= 5.5 + 4.2 = 9.7\) cm. (The value 1.3 cm is the difference of the radii, which applies to circles touching internally.)

stem: A line makes an angle of \(45^\circ\) with the positive direction of X-axis. So the slope of the line is ________.
solution: **(C)** \(1\). Slope \(m = \tan\theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle the line makes with the positive direction of the X-axis. \(\therefore m = \tan 45^\circ = 1\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: The volume of a cube of side 2 cm is ________.
solution: **(D)** 8 cm\(^3\). Volume of a cube \(= l^3\). \(\therefore\) volume \(= 2^3 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8\) cm\(^3\).

stem: Find the diagonal of square whose side is 10 cm.
solution: Diagonal of a square \(= \sqrt{2} \times\) side (by Pythagoras theorem, \(d^2 = 10^2 + 10^2 = 200\)). \(\therefore d = \sqrt{200} = 10\sqrt{2}\) cm. Check: \((10\sqrt{2})^2 = 200 = 10^2 + 10^2\).

subtopic: Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles
stem: The ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles is \(3 : 5\), then find the ratio of their areas.
solution: The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides. \(\therefore\) ratio of areas \(= \dfrac{3^2}{5^2} = \dfrac{9}{25}\), i.e. \(9 : 25\).

stem: Find the slope of the line passing through the points \(A(2, 3)\) and \(B(4, 7)\).
solution: Slope \(= \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\). \(\therefore\) slope of line AB \(= \dfrac{7 - 3}{4 - 2} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\).

stem: If \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{7}{25}\), then find the value of \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\).
solution: \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}\). \(\therefore \operatorname{cosec}\theta = \dfrac{1}{7/25} = \dfrac{25}{7}\).

subtopic: Ratio of Areas of Two Triangles
stem: In the given figure, \(AR \perp BC\), \(AR \perp PQ\), then complete the activity for finding \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle APQ)}\).
solution: AR is the common height of \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle APQ\), and the ratio of the areas of two triangles is the ratio of the products of their bases and corresponding heights. \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle APQ)} = \dfrac{BC \times AR}{PQ \times AR}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle APQ)} = \dfrac{BC}{PQ}\).
figureNote: triangle ABC with P, R, Q on base BC (B-P-R-Q-C); AR perpendicular to BC (right-angle mark at R); segments AP and AQ drawn, p-02

stem: In the following figure, seg PS is a tangent segment, line PR is a secant. If \(PQ = 3.6\), \(QR = 6.4\), then find PS by completing the following activity.
solution: \(PS^2 = PQ \times PR\) (tangent secant segments theorem). \(\therefore PS^2 = PQ \times (PQ + QR)\). \(\therefore PS^2 = 3.6 \times (3.6 + 6.4)\). \(\therefore PS^2 = 3.6 \times 10 = 36\). \(\therefore PS = 6\). Check: \(6^2 = 36 = 3.6 \times 10\).
figureNote: circle with external point P; secant from P cuts the circle at Q (near) and R (far); tangent from P touches the circle at S, p-03

subtopic: Area of Sector and Segment of a Circle
stem: Measure of an arc of a circle is \(90^\circ\) and its radius is 14 cm. Complete the following activity to find the length of an arc.
solution: Length of an arc \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r\) (formula). \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14\). \(= \dfrac{1}{4} \times 88\). \(\therefore\) length of an arc \(= 22\) cm. Check: the full circumference is \(2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 = 88\) cm, and a \(90^\circ\) arc is one quarter of it.

subtopic: Property of an Angle Bisector of a Triangle
stem: In the following figure, in \(\triangle LMN\), ray MT bisects \(\angle LMN\). If \(LM = 6\), \(MN = 10\), \(TN = 8\), then find LT.
solution: By the property of an angle bisector of a triangle, \(\dfrac{LM}{MN} = \dfrac{LT}{TN}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{LT}{8}\). \(\therefore LT = \dfrac{6 \times 8}{10} = 4.8\). Check: \(\dfrac{4.8}{8} = 0.6 = \dfrac{6}{10}\).
figureNote: triangle LMN with ray MT bisecting angle LMN (equal-angle dots at M), T on side LN; LM = 6, MN = 10, TN = 8 marked, p-04

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: Find surface area of sphere of radius 7 cm.
solution: Surface area of a sphere \(= 4\pi r^2\). \(= 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 4 \times 22 \times 7\). \(\therefore\) surface area \(= 616\) cm\(^2\).

stem: In the following figure, \(m(\text{arc } NS) = 125^\circ\), \(m(\text{arc } EF) = 37^\circ\). Find \(m\angle NMS\).
solution: Chords FS and EN intersect at M inside the circle. The measure of an angle formed by two chords intersecting inside a circle is half the sum of the measures of the arcs intercepted by the angle and its opposite angle. \(\therefore m\angle NMS = \dfrac{1}{2}[m(\text{arc } NS) + m(\text{arc } EF)] = \dfrac{1}{2}(125^\circ + 37^\circ) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 162^\circ = 81^\circ\).
figureNote: circle with chords FS and EN intersecting at M inside it; F and E on the left of the circle, N and S on the right, p-05

stem: Find the co-ordinates of midpoint of the segment joining the points \(P(22, 20)\) and \(Q(0, 16)\).
solution: By the midpoint formula, midpoint \(= \left(\dfrac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \dfrac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{22 + 0}{2}, \dfrac{20 + 16}{2}\right)\). \(\therefore\) midpoint of seg PQ \(= (11, 18)\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: Find the volume of a cone if radius of its base is 7 cm and its perpendicular height is 15 cm.
solution: Volume of a cone \(= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). \(= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 \times 15 = 22 \times 7 \times 5\). \(\therefore\) volume of the cone \(= 770\) cm\(^3\).

stem: If \(\tan\theta = 1\), then find the value of \(\dfrac{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}{\sec\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta}\) by completing the following activity.
solution: \(\tan\theta = 1\) (given). But \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\). \(\therefore \theta = 45^\circ\). \(\therefore \dfrac{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}{\sec\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta} = \dfrac{\sin 45^\circ + \cos 45^\circ}{\sec 45^\circ + \operatorname{cosec} 45^\circ} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}}{2\sqrt{2}}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}{\sec\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta} = \dfrac{1}{2}\). Check: \(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \div 2\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2} \times 2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

stem: In the following figure, point O is the centre of the circle and length of chord AB is equal to the radius of the circle. Find the measures of: (i) \(\angle AOB\) (ii) arc AB (iii) \(\angle ACB\) by completing the activity.
solution: In \(\triangle AOB\), \(AO = OB = AB\) (radii, and chord AB equals the radius). \(\therefore \triangle AOB\) is an equilateral triangle. \(\therefore m\angle AOB = 60^\circ\). \(m\angle AOB = m(\text{arc } AB) = 60^\circ\) (definition of measure of an arc). \(m\angle ACB = \dfrac{1}{2} \times m(\text{arc } AB)\) (inscribed angle theorem) \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 60^\circ\). \(\therefore m\angle ACB = 30^\circ\). Hence (i) \(m\angle AOB = 60^\circ\), (ii) \(m(\text{arc } AB) = 60^\circ\), (iii) \(m\angle ACB = 30^\circ\).
figureNote: circle with centre O; chord AB near the bottom with radii OA and OB forming triangle AOB; inscribed angle ACB with C at the top of the circle, p-07

stem: Find co-ordinates of point P, if P divides the line segment joining the points \(A(-1, 7)\) and \(B(4, -3)\) in the ratio \(2 : 3\).
solution: Let \(P(x, y)\). Here \((x_1, y_1) = (-1, 7)\), \((x_2, y_2) = (4, -3)\), \(m : n = 2 : 3\). By the section formula, \(x = \dfrac{mx_2 + nx_1}{m + n} = \dfrac{2 \times 4 + 3 \times (-1)}{2 + 3} = \dfrac{8 - 3}{5} = 1\) and \(y = \dfrac{my_2 + ny_1}{m + n} = \dfrac{2 \times (-3) + 3 \times 7}{2 + 3} = \dfrac{-6 + 21}{5} = 3\). \(\therefore\) the co-ordinates of P are \((1, 3)\). Check: \(AP = \sqrt{2^2 + 4^2} = 2\sqrt{5}\) and \(PB = \sqrt{3^2 + 6^2} = 3\sqrt{5}\), so \(AP : PB = 2 : 3\).

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw a circle with centre O of radius 3.4 cm. Draw a chord MN of length 5.7 cm in it. Construct tangents at point M and N to the circle.
solution: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so the tangents at M and N are drawn perpendicular to the radii OM and ON. Steps of construction: (1) With centre O and radius 3.4 cm draw a circle. (2) Take any point M on the circle. With M as centre and radius 5.7 cm draw an arc cutting the circle at N, and draw chord MN (possible since \(5.7 < 6.8\), the diameter). (3) Draw seg OM and seg ON. (4) At M draw line \(l \perp\) seg OM. (5) At N draw line \(m \perp\) seg ON. Lines \(l\) and \(m\) are the required tangents to the circle at M and N.

stem: A storm broke a tree and the treetop rested 20 m from the base of the tree, making an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the horizontal. Find the height of the tree.
solution: Let AB be the tree, broken at C so that part CB stands vertically and the broken part CA (= CD) touches the ground at D. Then \(\triangle CBD\) is right-angled at B, \(BD = 20\) m and \(\angle CDB = 60^\circ\). \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{CB}{BD}\), so \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{CB}{20}\) and \(CB = 20\sqrt{3}\) m. \(\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{BD}{CD}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{20}{CD}\) and \(CD = 40\) m. Height of the tree \(= CB + CD\). \(\therefore\) height of the tree \(= 20\sqrt{3} + 40 = 20(\sqrt{3} + 2)\) m (about 74.6 m, taking \(\sqrt{3} = 1.73\)). Check: \(CB^2 + BD^2 = 1200 + 400 = 1600 = 40^2 = CD^2\).

stem: Prove that, 'In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of remaining two sides'.
solution: Given: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\). To prove: \(AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2\). Construction: Draw seg \(BD \perp\) side AC, with A-D-C. Proof: In right-angled \(\triangle ABC\), seg \(BD \perp\) hypotenuse AC. \(\therefore \triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADB \sim \triangle BDC\) (similarity in right-angled triangles). From \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADB\): \(\dfrac{AB}{AD} = \dfrac{AC}{AB}\) (corresponding sides of similar triangles), so \(AB^2 = AD \times AC\) ...(I). From \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle BDC\): \(\dfrac{BC}{DC} = \dfrac{AC}{BC}\), so \(BC^2 = DC \times AC\) ...(II). Adding (I) and (II): \(AB^2 + BC^2 = AD \times AC + DC \times AC = AC(AD + DC) = AC \times AC\) (since A-D-C, \(AD + DC = AC\)). \(\therefore AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2\).

stem: \(\triangle ABC\) has sides of length 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm while \(\triangle PQR\) has perimeter of 90 cm. If \(\triangle ABC\) is similar to \(\triangle PQR\), then find the length of corresponding sides of \(\triangle PQR\).
solution: Perimeter of \(\triangle ABC = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15\) cm. The corresponding sides of similar triangles are in proportion, so the ratio of their perimeters equals the ratio of their corresponding sides. \(\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{BC}{QR} = \dfrac{AC}{PR} = \dfrac{15}{90} = \dfrac{1}{6}\). Taking \(AB = 4\), \(BC = 5\), \(AC = 6\): \(PQ = 6 \times 4 = 24\) cm, \(QR = 6 \times 5 = 30\) cm, \(PR = 6 \times 6 = 36\) cm. \(\therefore\) the sides of \(\triangle PQR\) are 24 cm, 30 cm and 36 cm. Check: \(24 + 30 + 36 = 90\) cm.

stem: \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PBR\), \(BC = 8\) cm, \(AC = 10\) cm, \(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(\dfrac{BC}{BR} = \dfrac{5}{4}\), then construct \(\triangle PBR\).
solution: Rough figure and calculation: in right-angled \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB = \sqrt{10^2 - 8^2} = 6\) cm. Since \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PBR\), \(\dfrac{AB}{PB} = \dfrac{BC}{BR} = \dfrac{AC}{PR} = \dfrac{5}{4}\), so \(BR = \dfrac{4}{5} \times 8 = 6.4\) cm, \(PB = \dfrac{4}{5} \times 6 = 4.8\) cm and \(PR = \dfrac{4}{5} \times 10 = 8\) cm. Steps of construction: (1) Draw seg \(BC = 8\) cm. (2) At B draw a ray perpendicular to BC. (3) With C as centre and radius 10 cm draw an arc cutting this ray at A; join AC. This is \(\triangle ABC\). (4) Draw ray BX making an acute angle with BC on the side opposite to A. (5) On ray BX mark points \(B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4, B_5\) such that \(BB_1 = B_1B_2 = B_2B_3 = B_3B_4 = B_4B_5\). (6) Join \(B_5C\). Through \(B_4\) draw a line parallel to \(B_5C\) meeting BC at R. (7) Through R draw a line parallel to CA meeting BA at P. \(\therefore \triangle PBR\) is the required triangle, with \(BR = 6.4\) cm, \(PB = 4.8\) cm, \(PR = 8\) cm and \(\angle B = 90^\circ\).

stem: In the following figure \(\triangle ABC\) is an isosceles triangle with perimeter 44 cm. The base BC is of length 12 cm. Side AB and AC are congruent. A circle touches the three sides of triangle as shown. Find the length of tangent segment from A to circle.
solution: \(AB + AC + BC = 44\) and \(AB = AC\), so \(2AB + 12 = 44\) and \(AB = AC = 16\) cm. Let the circle touch AB at P, AC at Q and BC at R. Tangent segments drawn from an external point to a circle are congruent, so \(AP = AQ\), \(BP = BR\) and \(CQ = CR\). Since \(AB = AC\) and \(AP = AQ\), \(AB - AP = AC - AQ\), i.e. \(BP = CQ\); hence \(BR = CR = \dfrac{12}{2} = 6\) cm and \(BP = 6\) cm. \(\therefore AP = AB - BP = 16 - 6 = 10\) cm. The length of the tangent segment from A to the circle is 10 cm. Check: \(AP + AQ + BR + RC + BP + CQ = 10 + 10 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 44\) cm.
figureNote: isosceles triangle ABC (apex A) with its incircle touching AB at P, AC at Q and BC at R, centre dot shown, p-09

context: Draw right-angled \(\triangle ABC\) of lengths of sides are 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Draw median on the hypotenuse of \(\triangle ABC\). Then:
stem: Measure the length of median and write it.
solution: Since \(3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5^2\), the triangle is right-angled with hypotenuse 5 cm. Construction: draw seg \(BC = 4\) cm, draw a ray perpendicular to BC at B, and mark A on it with \(AB = 3\) cm; join AC (it measures 5 cm). Find the midpoint D of hypotenuse AC by drawing its perpendicular bisector, and join BD. BD is the median on the hypotenuse. \(\therefore\) on measuring, the median \(BD = 2.5\) cm.

context: Draw right-angled \(\triangle ABC\) of lengths of sides are 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Draw median on the hypotenuse of \(\triangle ABC\). Then:
stem: By obeserving lengths of median and hypotenuse write your observations.
solution: Median \(BD = 2.5\) cm and hypotenuse \(AC = 5\) cm, so \(BD = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AC\). Observation: in a right-angled triangle, the median drawn to the hypotenuse is half the hypotenuse. So \(AD = DC = BD = 2.5\) cm, and the midpoint of the hypotenuse is equidistant from all three vertices.

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
context: Observe the given figure and answer the following questions:
stem: How many surfaces does a solid cone have?
solution: A solid cone has two surfaces: one curved surface and one flat circular surface (its base).
figureNote: right circular cone with vertex P, base diameter AB and centre O of the base; PO perpendicular to AB (right-angle mark at O), p-10

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
context: Observe the given figure and answer the following questions:
stem: What are the names of slant height and perpendicular height in the given figure?
solution: In the figure, P is the vertex and O is the centre of the base. Slant height: seg PA (or seg PB), the distance from the vertex to a point on the edge of the base. Perpendicular height: seg PO, the perpendicular from the vertex to the centre of the base.
figureNote: right circular cone with vertex P, base diameter AB and centre O of the base; PO perpendicular to AB (right-angle mark at O), p-10

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
context: Observe the given figure and answer the following questions:
stem: If slant height of solid cone is 10 cm and perpendicular height is 8 cm, then find diameter of base of solid cone?
solution: In right-angled \(\triangle POA\), \(\angle POA = 90^\circ\), slant height \(l = PA = 10\) cm, height \(h = PO = 8\) cm and radius \(r = OA\). By Pythagoras theorem, \(l^2 = r^2 + h^2\), so \(r^2 = 10^2 - 8^2 = 100 - 64 = 36\) and \(r = 6\) cm. Diameter \(= 2r\). \(\therefore\) diameter of the base \(= 2 \times 6 = 12\) cm. Check: \(6^2 + 8^2 = 36 + 64 = 100 = 10^2\).
figureNote: right circular cone with vertex P, base diameter AB and centre O of the base; PO perpendicular to AB (right-angle mark at O), p-10
